title: PMC standing committee orders daily anti-mosquito drives amid dengue & chikungunya fears, seeks quick dep - The Times of India

analysis.time: PMC standing committee directed daily anti-mosquito drives on Thursday, August 27, 2026, amid fears of a rise in dengue and chikungunya cases. The directive was issued in response to growing complaints from residents about fever and other health-related issues.
analysis.location_and_population: The action was taken in Pune, India, targeting the local population and focusing on vulnerable locations where mosquito breeding is a concern.
analysis.event: The Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) standing committee ordered daily anti-mosquito spraying and fogging drives to combat the potential spread of dengue and chikungunya. Health inspectors were instructed to visit housing societies and open plots to eliminate stagnant water, a key mosquito-breeding source.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: PMC data indicates that 1,708 notices were issued and Rs 2.65 lakh in fines collected this year after detecting mosquito-breeding sites. The committee also sought to expedite the appointment of 265 contractual workers to strengthen mosquito-control measures, citing concerns over contaminated drain water mixing with potable water and the impact of continuous rainfall and fluctuating temperatures in August.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The PMC standing committee has directed anti-mosquito drives and requested explanations for delays in hiring additional workers. The response is ongoing, with officials stating that 150 permanent posts are already filled, but the proposal for 265 contractual employees remains pending.

analysis.brief_en: In response to fears of a potential rise in dengue and chikungunya cases, the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) standing committee ordered daily anti-mosquito spraying and fogging drives on August 27, 2026. The directive was issued to address growing concerns about stagnant water, a key mosquito-breeding source, and to eliminate health risks associated with these diseases. Health inspectors were instructed to visit housing societies and open plots to ensure that water accumulation was promptly addressed. The committee also sought to expedite the appointment of 265 contractual workers to enhance mosquito-control efforts, citing irregularities in spraying operations and the impact of continuous rainfall and fluctuating temperatures in August. PMC officials mentioned that 150 permanent posts are already filled, but the proposal for additional workers remains pending. The action is part of an ongoing response to mitigate the spread of chikungunya and dengue, with the goal of protecting public health in Pune.
